correctness.rationale: The source's exhaustive scalar calculus identifies every internal one-one degree with a unique positive dyadic and makes direct sum correspond to addition. The Grothendieck completion is therefore the dyadic additive group. Any additive automorphism F is determined by c=F(1); divisibility by every power of two forces F(q)=cq on all positive dyadics. Surjectivity holds exactly for positive units c of Z[1/2], namely powers of two, yielding automorphism group Z and trivial stabilizer of the base scalar 1.

value.rationale: Direct sum is a canonical operation on reducibility degrees. Retaining it converts the source's exact dense-order witness into a concrete ordered cancellative semigroup, identifies its universal group completion, and shows that the enormous symmetry of the rational order collapses to a countable dyadic-rescaling group. The trivial stabilizer of the constructed base degree gives a sharp algebraic rigidity statement that is invisible in the source's headline order theorem.
